newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Astra shareholder denies to sell stake.
newsitem.headline: Astra shareholder denies to sell stake.

text.p: Indonesian timber tycoon Projogo Pangestu has denied speculation that he will sell his 10.68 percent stake in the country's largest vehicle manufacturer Astra International, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Friday.
"I plan to keep my shares in Astra as long as the company is in operation. I guarantee Astra has very good prospects," he was quoted as saying.

Bisnis Indonesia reported last week that Siti Hardianti Rukmana, President Suharto's eldest daughter and the head of toll-road operator Pt Citra Marga, was in talks with Pangestu to buy out his stake.

The report came amid a strong surge in Astra prices as rumours spread that a takeover bid was in progress. Tobacco magnate Putera Sampoerna, who heads cigarette company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, has said he now effectively controls a 12.66 percent stake in Astra.
Prajogo also denied market talk that his flagship company Barito Pacific Timber has financial problems, Bisnis Indonesia said.

On Thursday, privately-owned PT Chandra Asri Petrochemical Centre, Indonesia's only olefins producer, denied reports that Pangestu was in talks with Malaysian state oil company Petronas to sell his stake in the company. Pangestu is said to hold about 10 percent of Chandra Asri.
Astra was trading at 3,575 rupiah, down 25, on Friday. it had reached a peak of 3,825 last week at the height of the takeover talk.
